akhfash:1-3.t:
He said ﴿حـمۤ﴾ ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ﴾ ﴿غَافِرِ ٱلذَّنبِ وَقَابِلِ ٱلتَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ ٱلْعِقَابِ﴾: this is as a badal (substitute), because this is the attribute. As for ﴿غَافِرِ ٱلذَّنبِ وَقَابِلِ ٱلتَّوْبِ﴾, it may be definite, because you say: "هذا ضاربُ زيدٍ مُقْبِلاً" (this is the striker of Zayd, coming forward) when you do not intend tanwīn by it. Then He said ﴿ذِي ٱلطَّوْلِ﴾, which may be a badal or an attribute. In it the nominative is allowed as a mubtadaʾ, and the accusative as the khabar of a definite, except in ﴿ذِي ٱلطَّوْلِ﴾, for there the accusative as the khabar of a definite is not possible, because it is definite. "التَوْبُ" is the collective of "التَوْبَةِ" (repentance); one says "عَوْمَةٌ" and "عَوْمٌ", as in "عَوْمِ السَّفِينَةِ" (the floating of the ship). The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is poetic witness no. 265]:
عَوْم السَّفِينِ فَلَمَّا حالَ دُونَهُمُ * فَيْدُ القُرَيَّاتِ فالفِتْكَانُ فالكَرَمُ
(Like the floating of ships; then, when Fayd of al-Qurayyāt, then al-Fitkān, then al-Karam came between them and us…)
«[Translator's note: "the accusative as the khabar of a definite" is understood here as the accusative of a ḥāl.]»

akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿وَهَمَّتْ كُـلُّ أُمَّةٍ بِرَسُولِهِمْ﴾: He used the plural (pronoun) referring to "الكُلَّ" because "الكُلَّ" is masculine and its meaning is that of a group.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ﴾, i.e. because they are, or in that they are; ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ is not in the position of an object. It is not like your saying "أَأَحَقَّت أنهم"; were it so, it would be "أَحَقَّتْ أَنَّهُمْ" (it made it due that they…).

akhfash:7-7.t: And He said ﴿وَسِعْتَ كُـلَّ شَيْءٍ رَّحْمَةً وَعِلْماً﴾: its accusative is like the accusative in "لَكَ مِثْلُه عَبْداً" (you have the like of him as a slave), because you made "وسعت" (You encompassed) act on "كلّ شَيْءٍ" (everything), which is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the agent being the tāʾ, and you brought "the mercy" and "the knowledge" as an explanation (tamyīz (specification)) from which the verb is occupied, just as "المِثْلُ" is occupied with the hāʾ; for that reason you put it in the accusative, likening it to the object after the agent.

akhfash:10-10.t: And He said ﴿يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾: this lām is the lām of the mubtadaʾ (lām al-ibtidāʾ), as though "they are called out to", and it is said to them — because calling is a saying. Its like in iʿrāb: one says "لَزَيْدٌ أَفضْلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو" (Zayd is surely better than ʿAmr).

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿رَفِيعُ ٱلدَّرَجَاتِ ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ﴾: "رفيع" is [nominative] as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The accusative would be allowed if it were, in speech, by way of praise.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ﴾: He annexed (يوم) to the meaning (of the clause), and for that reason "the day" does not take tanwīn, as He said ﴿يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾. And He said ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ﴾, its meaning being "this is the day of their trial". But since He began with the noun (هم) and it remained (nominative), He could not put it in the genitive, and the annexation was in meaning to "the trial". This happens only when "اليَوْم" (the day) has the meaning of "إِذْ" (when); otherwise it is ugly.
Do you not see that you say "لَقِيتُكَ زَمَنَ زَيْدٌ أَمِيرٌ" (I met you at the time when Zayd was commander), i.e. when Zayd was commander; but if you said "أَلْقَاكَ زَمَنَ زيد أَميرْ" (I will meet you at the time when Zayd is commander) it would not be good.
And He said ﴿لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾: this is on an implied "He says".

akhfash:18-18.t: And He said ﴿إِذِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلْحَنَاجِرِ كَاظِمِينَ﴾: ﴿كَاظِمِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He meant "the hearts are at the throats in this state".

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿عَلَىٰ كُـلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ﴾: whoever puts tanwīn (on قلب) makes "the arrogant, the tyrant" an attribute of it, and whoever does not put tanwīn annexes "the heart" to "the arrogant".

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿يٰهَامَانُ ٱبْنِ لِي﴾: some put ḍamma on the nūn, as though he made it follow the ḍamma of the nūn in ﴿هامان﴾, just as they said "مِنْتِنٌ" (stinking), putting kasra on the mīm because of the kasra on the tāʾ, with a vowelless letter between them, which did not form a barrier. Likewise the bāʾ did not form a barrier in His word ﴿ابنِ لي﴾.

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿وَحَاقَ بِآلِ فِرْعَوْنَ سُوۤءُ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾ ﴿ٱلنَّـارِ﴾: if you wish you make ﴿النُارِ﴾ a badal (substitute) for ﴿سوءُ العذاب﴾ and put it in the nominative by ﴿حاقَ﴾; if you wish you make it an explanation and put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as though you said: "it is the Fire"; and if you wish you put it in the genitive, making ﴿النار﴾ a badal for ﴿العذاب﴾, as though you meant: "the evil of the Fire".

akhfash:46-46.t:
And He said ﴿غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْخِلُوۤاْ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾: in it is an implied "it will be said to them: enter, O family of Pharaoh". Some read ﴿أَدْخِلُوا﴾ with a disjunctive hamza, making it from "أَدْخَلَ يُدْخِلُ" (to cause to enter). And He said ﴿غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ﴾: it is only a maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say: "آتِيهِ ظَلاماً" (I come to him in the dark), making it an adverbial (ẓarf); it is a maṣdar made into a ẓarf. If you said "مَوْعِدُكَ غَدْرَةٌ" or "مَوْعِدُكَ ظلامٌ" (your appointment is a morning / darkness) in the nominative, as you say "مَوْعِدكَ يومُ الجمعة" (your appointment is Friday), it would not be good, because these maṣdars and the like of them, such as "سَحَر" (the pre-dawn), are used only as adverbials, and the adverbial is altogether not fully declinable.
And He said ﴿أَدْخِلُوۤاْ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾, and He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي ٱلدَّرْكِ ٱلأَسْفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾; so it is possible that the family of Pharaoh will be made to enter with the hypocrites into the lowest depth, and that is the severest punishment.
As for His word ﴿فَإِنِّيۤ أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَاباً لاَّ أُعَذِّبُهُ أَحَداً مِّنَ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, it means: "with which I do not punish anyone of the world of the people of his time".

akhfash:47-47.t: And He said ﴿كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعاً﴾ because "التَبَعَ" (follower) can be singular and plural, and it is pluralised as "أَتْباع".

akhfash:48-48.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيهَآ﴾: He made ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ a noun that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), as you say: "إِنَّا كُلُّنا فيها" (we are all in it).

akhfash:51-51.t: And He said ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلأَشْهَادُ﴾, and ﴿تَقُومُ﴾: both are allowed. Likewise for every plural, masculine or feminine, of human beings: masculine and feminine are both allowed in its verb.

akhfash:55-55.t: And He said ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْعَشِيِّ وَٱلإِبْكَارِ﴾: He means "in the early morning". You may say "بالدارِ زَيْدٌ" (at the house is Zayd), meaning "Zayd is in the house".

akhfash:60-60.t: And He said ﴿ٱدْعُونِيۤ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾: His word ﴿أَسْتَجِبْ﴾ is only (of the form) "أَفْعَلُ"; this alif is other than the connective alif. Do you not see that you say: "بِعْتَ" "تَبِيعُ" (you sold, you sell), then you say "أَبيعُ" (I sell), and an alif comes in it for "أَفْعَلُ"? It is the counterpart of the yāʾ and tāʾ in "يَفْعَلُ" and "تَفْعَلُ". You make disjunctive (the hamza of) everything of the form "أَفْعَلُ", whether in joining or in separation.

akhfash:79-79.t: And He said ﴿لِتَرْكَـبُواْ مِنْهَا﴾, as though He implied "something".
